item.content:encoded:
Are you passionate about history, gender studies, colonial societies, archival research, or digital humanities? Erasmus University Rotterdam is offering an exciting fully funded PhD opportunity for highly motivated researchers interested in investigating the transimperial history of women’s work between 1600 and 1900.

The Erasmus School of History, Culture and Communication (ESHCC) is seeking two PhD candidates to join an ambitious research project examining how European colonial expansion influenced ideas, practices, and experiences surrounding women’s labour across different regions of the world.

The successful candidates will become part of an interdisciplinary and internationally oriented research team led by Dr. Natália da Silva Perez. The project combines traditional historical and archival research with innovative computational approaches, including handwritten text recognition, multilingual datasets, digital humanities methods, natural language processing, statistical analysis, and qualitative historical research.

The positions provide an exceptional opportunity for emerging scholars to pursue doctoral research while receiving a competitive monthly salary, professional development opportunities, extensive employment benefits, research experience, teaching exposure, and access to an international academic environment in Rotterdam, the Netherlands.

About the Erasmus University Rotterdam PhD Research Project

The PhD project focuses on the relationship between European colonial expansion and changing ideas about women’s work between 1600 and 1900.

European colonialism created extensive political, economic, social, and cultural connections between European metropolitan centres and territories across Africa, the Americas, and other parts of the world. These connections influenced how labour was organised, represented, regulated, and understood.

Women played crucial roles within colonial and transimperial economies and societies. However, ideas about women’s work were often shaped by gender, race, class, colonial power, slavery, migration, and social hierarchies.

This research project seeks to investigate these complex historical relationships by examining both normative ideas about gendered labour and the lived experiences of women.

Rather than studying colonial societies in isolation, the project adopts a transimperial perspective. This approach explores how ideas, people, texts, institutions, and understandings of labour moved between different colonial territories and European metropolitan centres.

The selected PhD candidates will conduct independent doctoral research while contributing to a broader collaborative project.

The research will focus on one of two historical cases:

  1. Pernambuco
  2. Atlantic Africa, including potential research areas such as Senegambia, the Gold Coast, or Angola

Through these historical cases, the PhD researchers will explore important questions surrounding women’s labour, colonial societies, gender relations, and the circulation of ideas across imperial boundaries.

Understanding the Transimperial History of Women’s Work

The central objective of the project is to understand how women’s lived experiences of work either conformed to or diverged from dominant ideas about gendered labour.

Historical societies often developed expectations regarding what types of work women should perform. However, these expectations did not always reflect the realities of women’s everyday lives.

Women participated in numerous forms of economic, domestic, agricultural, commercial, and social labour. Their work could be influenced by factors including:

  • Gender
  • Colonial rule
  • Social class
  • Race
  • Enslavement
  • Migration
  • Family structures
  • Economic systems
  • Religious institutions
  • Legal regulations
  • Cultural traditions

The research project will investigate how ideas about women’s work circulated between European metropolitan centres and colonial territories.

By examining archival records from multiple regions and imperial contexts, researchers will be able to explore similarities, differences, exchanges, and transformations in historical understandings of gendered labour.

This makes the PhD particularly relevant for scholars interested in:

  • Colonial history
  • Early modern history
  • Women’s history
  • Gender history
  • African history
  • Atlantic history
  • Labour history
  • Social history
  • Digital humanities
  • Historical archives
  • Computational research methods
  • Intersectionality
  • Social reproduction theory

Research Areas Available for PhD Candidates

Applicants will be expected to focus their doctoral research on one of the project’s two major historical cases.

1. Pernambuco

One possible research focus is Pernambuco, a historically significant region in Brazil with a complex colonial past.

Researchers choosing this case may investigate historical sources relating to women’s work, labour systems, colonial societies, economic structures, and the circulation of ideas between Pernambuco and European metropolitan centres.

Applicants interested in the Pernambuco case may benefit from knowledge of languages such as:

  • Portuguese
  • Dutch
  • Spanish

Depending on their proposed research direction, candidates may also be encouraged to develop additional linguistic skills relevant to the archival material.

2. Atlantic Africa

The second research focus concerns Atlantic Africa.

Potential geographical areas may include:

  • Senegambia
  • The Gold Coast
  • Angola

This research case offers an opportunity to investigate women’s work and gendered labour within historically interconnected African and Atlantic worlds.

Researchers may examine the movement of people, ideas, economic systems, and institutional practices across African regions, colonial territories, and European metropolitan centres.

Relevant archival languages may include:

  • Portuguese
  • Dutch
  • French
  • English
  • Danish

Candidates are not necessarily expected to possess expertise in every language listed. However, strong knowledge of at least one language relevant to the chosen historical case is required, and willingness to develop additional language skills will be viewed positively.

What Will the Selected PhD Candidates Do?

The successful candidates will undertake independent doctoral research while contributing to the wider collaborative project.

The PhD programme is designed to combine traditional historical research with modern computational and digital methodologies.

Selected researchers will be expected to carry out several important academic and research activities.

Build and Curate Historical Datasets

One of the major responsibilities will involve contributing to the development of multilingual and transimperial historical datasets.

These datasets will focus on evidence relating to women’s work and gendered labour.

The materials may include:

  • Handwritten archival documents
  • Printed historical sources
  • Multilingual texts
  • Colonial records
  • Historical correspondence
  • Administrative documents
  • Other relevant primary sources

Researchers will contribute to the organisation and curation of these materials across different geographical locations and historical periods.

The project is particularly innovative because it combines historical evidence from multiple imperial and linguistic contexts.

Conduct Archival Research

Archival research will form a central component of the doctoral project.

PhD candidates will identify, examine, interpret, and analyse primary historical materials relevant to their selected research case.

Applicants will also be required to demonstrate an awareness of relevant archives when applying for the position.

As part of the application, candidates must identify two archives they intend to consult and explain why these archives are important for their proposed historical research.

Work with Multilingual Historical Texts

The project involves historical materials written in multiple languages.

Depending on the selected research case and linguistic expertise, researchers may work with texts in:

  • Portuguese
  • Dutch
  • French
  • English
  • Spanish
  • Danish

This multilingual dimension is particularly important because transimperial history requires researchers to examine connections that cross national, linguistic, and imperial boundaries.

Candidates who are willing to develop additional language skills relevant to the project will be positively considered.

Use Transkribus for Historical Text Transcription

The PhD candidates will work with Transkribus, a platform commonly used for the transcription and analysis of historical handwritten documents.

Researchers may use handwritten text recognition technologies to convert archival documents into searchable and analysable text.

However, automated transcription is not always perfect.

Candidates will therefore also be expected to manually review and correct transcription results.

This combination of digital technology and human expertise provides an opportunity to develop advanced skills in computational historical research.

Conduct Qualitative Historical Analysis

The project incorporates qualitative and interpretivist approaches to historical research.

PhD candidates may analyse historical evidence through theoretical perspectives including:

  • Interpretivist approaches
  • Social reproduction theory
  • Intersectionality

These approaches can help researchers understand how historical experiences were shaped by multiple forms of social difference and power.

For example, women’s experiences of work may have differed depending on factors such as social position, ethnicity, colonial status, enslavement, family background, geographical location, and access to economic resources.

Apply Computational and Quantitative Methods

The doctoral researchers will also use computational, digital humanities, and statistical approaches.

Potential methodological areas include:

  • Handwritten text recognition
  • Natural language processing
  • Corpus-based text analysis
  • Statistical analysis
  • Digital humanities
  • Computational historical research
  • Dataset development
  • Quantitative analysis

Candidates do not necessarily need to be experts in all these areas before beginning the PhD.

Applicants with experience and enthusiasm for computational methods are encouraged to apply, and candidates willing to develop their skills in these areas will also be considered.

Present Research at Academic Conferences

The successful candidates will be expected to communicate their research findings to the wider academic community.

This includes presenting research at relevant conferences.

Conference participation provides PhD researchers with opportunities to:

  • Share their research findings
  • Receive academic feedback
  • Connect with other scholars
  • Build international research networks
  • Develop academic presentation skills
  • Increase the visibility of their doctoral work

Publish Academic Research

The PhD dissertation will follow an article-based format.

Candidates will therefore be expected to publish research findings in peer-reviewed academic journals.

The publications may include:

  • Co-authored articles
  • Single-authored articles

This structure offers valuable experience in academic publishing and helps researchers develop a strong scholarly publication record during their doctoral studies.

Contribute to Teaching

The selected candidates will also participate in teaching activities within the History Department.

Teaching responsibilities can provide important professional experience for researchers interested in future academic careers.

Through teaching, doctoral candidates may strengthen their skills in:

  • Academic communication
  • Curriculum engagement
  • Student support
  • Presentation
  • Research dissemination
  • Higher education teaching

Who Can Apply for the Erasmus University Rotterdam PhD Position?

Erasmus University Rotterdam is seeking highly motivated candidates with strong academic backgrounds and an interest in interdisciplinary historical research.

The position is particularly suitable for applicants who want to combine historical scholarship with innovative digital and computational methodologies.

Academic Qualification Requirements

Applicants must hold, or be expected to complete before the starting date, a research master’s degree or another relevant master’s degree.

Relevant academic backgrounds may include:

  • History
  • Gender Studies
  • Digital Humanities
  • Early Modern Studies
  • Colonial Studies
  • African History
  • Atlantic History
  • Cultural History
  • Social History
  • Women’s Studies
  • Humanities
  • Other related disciplines

The master’s degree must be completed by the beginning of the appointment.

English Language Skills

Applicants must demonstrate excellent knowledge of English.

Strong English skills are required for:

  • Academic writing
  • Research communication
  • Conference presentations
  • Scholarly publishing
  • Collaboration within an international research team

Because the research environment is internationally oriented, the ability to communicate effectively in English is essential.

Additional Language Requirements

Candidates must have strong knowledge of at least one additional language relevant to archival research for their chosen historical case.

For applicants focusing on Pernambuco, relevant languages include:

  • Portuguese
  • Dutch
  • Spanish

For applicants focusing on Atlantic Africa, relevant languages include:

  • Portuguese
  • Dutch
  • French
  • English
  • Danish

The ability and willingness to develop additional language skills will also be considered an advantage.

Interest in Historical Research

Applicants should demonstrate an interest in or experience with areas such as:

  • Early modern history
  • Colonial history
  • Gender history
  • Women’s history
  • Colonial Atlantic history
  • Relations between colonies and European metropolitan centres

Candidates should be able to demonstrate how their previous academic training, research experience, or intellectual interests relate to the broader objectives of the project.

Interest in Digital and Computational Methods

The project strongly encourages candidates who have experience with or enthusiasm for computational and digital research methods.

Relevant skills may include experience with:

  • Handwritten text recognition
  • Digital humanities
  • Natural language processing
  • Statistics
  • Corpus analysis
  • Digital archives
  • Data analysis

However, applicants who do not yet have extensive technical experience may still be competitive if they demonstrate a strong willingness to learn and develop these skills.

Analytical and Academic Writing Skills

Strong analytical ability is essential.

Successful applicants should demonstrate:

  • Excellent academic writing skills
  • Intellectual curiosity
  • Critical thinking
  • Research independence
  • Methodological flexibility
  • Openness to experimentation

The PhD project involves combining multiple methodologies. Candidates should therefore be comfortable exploring new research approaches.

Ability to Work Independently and Collaboratively

Although each PhD candidate will conduct an independent research project, the positions are part of a collaborative research group.

Applicants should therefore be able to:

  • Work independently
  • Manage long-term research projects
  • Collaborate with colleagues
  • Participate in interdisciplinary discussions
  • Contribute to collective research activities

Cultural Sensitivity and Reflexivity

The project involves archival materials relating to enslaved and colonised peoples.

Candidates must therefore demonstrate cultural sensitivity and reflexivity when working with historical sources.

This requirement is important because historical archives often reflect unequal power relationships and may contain perspectives shaped by colonial institutions.

Researchers must approach such materials critically and responsibly.

Preferred Qualifications

Although not mandatory, several additional qualifications may strengthen an application.

These include:

Knowledge of Additional Languages

Candidates with working knowledge of additional project-relevant languages may have an advantage.

These languages may include:

  • Portuguese
  • Dutch
  • French
  • English
  • Spanish
  • Danish

Archival and Paleographic Research Experience

Experience working with historical manuscripts or archival materials is considered beneficial.

Relevant experience may include:

  • Reading historical documents
  • Paleography
  • Manuscript interpretation
  • Archival research
  • Primary source analysis

Qualitative Coding Experience

Experience with qualitative research methods and coding may also be useful.

Corpus-Based Text Analysis

Candidates with experience analysing large collections of texts may be particularly well positioned for the computational components of the project.

Theoretical Knowledge

Familiarity with the following theoretical approaches may be advantageous:

  • Intersectionality
  • Social reproduction theory
  • Interpretivist historical methods

Salary and Employment Conditions

The PhD candidates will receive employment under the Collective Labour Agreement for Dutch Universities, known as CAO-NU.

The position offers a competitive salary and a comprehensive package of employment benefits.

Monthly Salary

The gross monthly salary ranges from:

€3,204 to €4,051

The salary is based on a full-time appointment.

Employment Duration

The initial contract will be offered for one year.

Subject to a positive assessment, the appointment may be extended for an additional three years.

This provides the possibility of a four-year doctoral employment trajectory.

Working Hours

The position is full-time.

The appointment is:

1.0 FTE

The full-time working schedule is based on approximately 38 hours per week.

Expected Start Date

The expected starting date is:

26 October 2026

Alternatively, the start date may be agreed upon after this date.

Benefits of the Erasmus University Rotterdam PhD Position

Beyond the monthly salary, successful candidates will receive access to a wide range of employment benefits and professional development opportunities.

Work-Life Balance

Erasmus University Rotterdam provides several benefits intended to support employee well-being and work-life balance.

Depending on the employment arrangement and consultation with management, benefits include:

  • Opportunities for working from home
  • Extensive paid leave
  • 41 days of paid leave under a 40-hour contract
  • 8% holiday pay
  • An 8.3% end-of-year bonus
  • Discounts on subscriptions to on-campus sports facilities

Professional and Career Development

PhD candidates will have access to opportunities supporting professional development.

These include:

  • Development days
  • Personal career budget opportunities
  • Access to university resources
  • Free access to the university library
  • Opportunities to participate in academic research networks

The position provides a strong environment for developing expertise in historical research, archival methods, computational analysis, academic writing, publishing, and teaching.

Inclusive and Diverse Working Environment

Erasmus University Rotterdam promotes an inclusive and diverse workplace.

The university aims to create an environment where employees can bring their full identities and perspectives to their work.

The institution also supports various professional and community networks.

Employees may benefit from initiatives and networks such as:

  • Young@EUR
  • FAME
  • QuEUR

The university welcomes applicants from diverse backgrounds.

Pension and Insurance Benefits

Employees may receive access to:

  • A pension arrangement through ABP
  • University contributions toward pension benefits
  • Discounts on selected collective insurance arrangements

Travel and Remote Work Support

The university also provides compensation arrangements relating to:

  • Travel
  • Working from home
  • Home internet use

Family-Friendly Employment Support

EUR provides support for employees balancing professional responsibilities with family life.

Relevant benefits may include:

  • Partially paid parental leave
  • Fully paid additional birth leave for partners
  • Access to childcare facilities on campus

Support for International Employees

International applicants relocating to the Netherlands may be eligible for additional support.

Depending on individual eligibility requirements, this may include:

  • Potential access to the Dutch 30% tax ruling
  • Support through the Dual Career Programme
  • Assistance for partners seeking employment opportunities

About Erasmus University Rotterdam

Erasmus University Rotterdam is an internationally oriented research university located in Rotterdam, the Netherlands.

The university is known for its strong focus on education, research, international collaboration, and societal impact.

Its mission is centred on the idea of creating positive societal impact.

EUR has a large and diverse international academic community, including:

  • Approximately 4,100 academics and professionals
  • Nearly 33,000 students
  • Students and staff connected to more than 140 countries

The university operates under the guiding philosophy:

The Erasmian Way – Making Minds Matter

Its institutional values emphasise qualities such as:

  • Global citizenship
  • International connection
  • Entrepreneurship
  • Open-mindedness
  • Social involvement

Researchers and staff work across disciplines to address complex societal challenges.

Rotterdam’s international and cosmopolitan environment also provides an attractive setting for scholars interested in global, transnational, and historical research.

About the Erasmus School of History, Culture and Communication

The Erasmus School of History, Culture and Communication, commonly known as ESHCC, is part of Erasmus University Rotterdam.

The school operates at the intersection of the Humanities and Social Sciences.

ESHCC consists of three major departments:

  1. History
  2. Arts and Culture
  3. Media and Communication

The school provides an intellectually stimulating environment for Dutch and international students and researchers.

Its academic programmes include:

  • Bachelor’s programmes
  • Master’s programmes
  • Multiple specialised academic tracks
  • Erasmus Mundus programmes
  • Research master’s programmes

Many programmes are internationally oriented and taught in English.

The Derius Research Institute

ESHCC hosts Derius, the Erasmus Research Institute for Media, Culture and History.

Researchers associated with the institute conduct interdisciplinary research in areas including:

  • Media
  • Communication
  • Culture
  • History
  • Society

The research environment encourages interdisciplinary collaboration and seeks to increase the societal impact of academic research.

The school is located in the Van der Goot Building on Erasmus University’s Woudestein campus.

Documents Required for the Application

Applicants must submit their application by the stated deadline.

The application should include several important documents.

1. Curriculum Vitae

Candidates must submit an up-to-date CV.

The CV should ideally highlight relevant information such as:

  • Educational background
  • Master’s degree research
  • Research experience
  • Language skills
  • Archival experience
  • Digital humanities experience
  • Publications
  • Conference participation
  • Technical skills
  • Relevant professional or academic activities

2. Academic Writing Sample

Applicants must provide an excerpt from their master’s thesis.

Alternatively, candidates may submit another piece of academic writing that engages with primary sources.

The writing sample provides the selection committee with an opportunity to assess the applicant’s:

  • Research skills
  • Analytical ability
  • Academic writing
  • Use of sources
  • Methodological approach

3. Motivation Letter

Applicants must submit a motivation letter of no more than 1,200 words.

The motivation letter is an important component of the application and should clearly demonstrate the applicant’s suitability for the project.

The letter must address several specific areas.

General Experience and Project Relevance

Applicants should explain their academic and research experience and demonstrate how it relates to the broader PhD project.

Candidates should connect their previous work with areas such as:

  • History
  • Gender
  • Colonialism
  • Archival research
  • Digital humanities
  • Computational methods
  • Women’s labour

Choice of Historical Case

Applicants must clearly indicate which historical case they wish to research.

The available choices are:

  • Pernambuco
  • Atlantic Africa

Candidates should demonstrate that they have carefully considered their preferred research area.

Interest in the Selected Historical Case

Applicants must explain why their chosen historical case interests them.

A strong explanation could connect the proposed research area to:

  • Previous academic research
  • Master’s thesis work
  • Language skills
  • Historical interests
  • Career objectives
  • Knowledge of relevant archives

Relevant Language Skills

Candidates should clearly explain their language skills beyond English.

Applicants should demonstrate how these skills are relevant to their chosen historical case and proposed archival research.

Proposed Archives

One of the most important components of the motivation letter is the identification of two archives.

Applicants must:

  1. Identify two archives they intend to consult for primary sources.
  2. Explain why these archives are relevant to their selected historical case.
  3. Demonstrate how the archival materials could contribute to the proposed research.

This requirement means applicants should conduct preliminary research before submitting their application.

A strong application will demonstrate awareness of potential primary sources and archival collections.

Computational and Digital Methods

Applicants should explain their previous experience with computational or digital research methods.

Those without extensive experience should demonstrate openness and enthusiasm for learning new methodologies.

How to Prepare a Competitive Application

Applicants interested in this PhD opportunity should approach the application strategically.

Research the Historical Case Thoroughly

Before applying, candidates should investigate both available historical cases and determine which aligns most closely with their academic background.

Consider:

  • Your previous research experience
  • Your master’s thesis topic
  • Your language abilities
  • Your knowledge of relevant historical contexts
  • Availability of archival materials
  • Long-term research interests

Identify Relevant Archives

Because applicants must identify two archives, this step should not be left until the final stages of preparing the application.

Research:

  • National archives
  • Colonial archives
  • University collections
  • Digital archives
  • Historical manuscript collections
  • Libraries with relevant primary source materials

Consider what types of documents may help answer questions about women’s work and gendered labour.

Demonstrate Methodological Curiosity

This project combines traditional and innovative methods.

Applicants should demonstrate openness to interdisciplinary research.

Even if you do not have extensive technical expertise, you can strengthen your application by showing:

  • Curiosity about digital humanities
  • Willingness to learn computational methods
  • Experience working with digital research tools
  • Interest in data-driven historical research

Connect Your Background to the Project

Your application should clearly explain why your previous academic experiences have prepared you for this PhD.

Relevant experiences may include:

  • Master’s thesis research
  • Archival research
  • Historical research
  • Gender studies
  • Language studies
  • Data analysis
  • Digital humanities projects
  • Research assistant positions
  • Academic writing

Pay Attention to Language Requirements

Language skills are particularly important because the project involves multilingual archival research.

Clearly explain:

  • Languages you currently speak or read
  • Your level of proficiency
  • Previous experience using the language academically
  • How the language relates to your chosen historical case
  • Your willingness to acquire additional languages

Selection and Interview Process

Candidates who progress through the initial application stage may be invited for an interview.

The interviews are expected to take place online.

Expected Interview Period

Interviews are scheduled for:

Week 40 of 2026

This falls in early October 2026.

Candidates should therefore ensure that their contact details are accurate and monitor their email after submitting their application.

APPLY HERE

Important Dates

Applicants should carefully note the following dates:

Activity Date
Vacancy published 1 September 2026
Application deadline 20 September 2026
Expected online interviews Week 40 of 2026
Expected start date 26 October 2026 or later by agreement

Why You Should Consider Applying

This opportunity offers considerably more than a conventional doctoral programme.

The selected candidates will gain the opportunity to develop expertise at the intersection of historical research and emerging digital methodologies.

Some of the major advantages include:

  • Competitive monthly salary ranging from €3,204 to €4,051 gross
  • Potential four-year doctoral employment trajectory
  • Full-time funded academic position
  • Opportunity to conduct independent doctoral research
  • Research within an international university environment
  • Training in archival research
  • Experience with multilingual historical sources
  • Exposure to digital humanities methodologies
  • Opportunities to work with Transkribus
  • Development of computational research skills
  • Experience with qualitative and quantitative methods
  • Opportunities to publish peer-reviewed research
  • Conference presentation opportunities
  • Teaching experience
  • Extensive employment benefits
  • Professional development opportunities
  • Access to academic resources and libraries
  • Inclusive and internationally diverse working environment
  • Potential support for international relocation

The interdisciplinary nature of the project is particularly attractive for researchers who want to move beyond traditional disciplinary boundaries.

Candidates will have an opportunity to combine close reading of historical sources with computational approaches capable of analysing larger bodies of multilingual archival material.

Visit HERE to learn more about the Erasmus University Rotterdam PhD Candidate Position 2026.

Diversity and Equal Opportunity

Erasmus University Rotterdam welcomes applications from individuals with diverse backgrounds.

The university explicitly encourages applications regardless of:

  • Gender identity
  • Gender expression
  • Sexual orientation
  • Religion
  • Ethnicity
  • Age
  • Neurodiversity
  • Functional impairment
  • Citizenship
  • Other personal backgrounds

The institution aims to create an inclusive academic environment where diverse experiences and perspectives contribute to research and education.

International applicants are therefore encouraged to explore the opportunity.

Application Deadline

The deadline for submitting applications is: 20 September 2026

Applicants are encouraged to prepare and submit their documents early, particularly because the application requires careful preparation of a motivation letter, academic writing sample, language information, and preliminary archival research.

Late preparation may make it difficult to identify appropriate archives and develop a strong research-focused motivation letter.

Conclusion

The Erasmus University Rotterdam PhD Candidate position on the Transimperial History of Women’s Work presents an exceptional opportunity for emerging researchers interested in colonial history, gender history, women’s labour, Atlantic history, and digital humanities.

The project stands out because of its interdisciplinary methodology, combining traditional archival scholarship with computational analysis, multilingual historical research, handwritten text recognition, and quantitative methods.

Successful applicants will pursue independent doctoral research focusing on either Pernambuco or Atlantic Africa while contributing to a wider collaborative investigation into how European colonial expansion shaped ideas and realities surrounding women’s work between 1600 and 1900.

With a competitive salary of €3,204 to €4,051 gross per month, extensive employment benefits, opportunities for academic publishing and conference participation, and the possibility of a four-year doctoral trajectory, this position provides an excellent pathway for researchers seeking to build an international academic career.

Applicants with strong academic backgrounds, relevant language skills, an interest in colonial and gender history, and enthusiasm for innovative research methods should carefully consider applying. Since the application requires a well-developed motivation letter and preliminary identification of relevant archives, prospective candidates should begin preparing their materials as early as possible before the 20 September 2026 deadline.

item.content:encoded:
The Harvard Academy Scholars Program 2027–2028 is now accepting applications from outstanding early-career scholars who have recently completed, or are nearing completion of, a PhD or equivalent doctoral degree in the social sciences.

Hosted by the Harvard Academy for International and Area Studies at Harvard University, the Academy Scholars Program is a prestigious two-year, in-residence postdoctoral fellowship designed for researchers whose work combines strong social science scholarship with deep knowledge of countries or regions outside the United States and Canada.

The programme provides selected scholars with substantial financial support, research assistance, mentoring, access to Harvard’s academic community and dedicated time to develop ambitious research and publication projects. For the 2027–2028 cohort, the application deadline is September 18, 2026, at 11:59 PM EDT.

The Harvard Academy is highly selective. It receives more than 500 applications in many years and normally selects only five or six Academy Scholars for each cohort.

About the Harvard Academy Scholars Program

The Harvard Academy for International and Area Studies is housed within the Weatherhead Center for International Affairs at Harvard University.

Its mission is to promote innovative social science research while deepening understanding of the experiences and practices of different regions and countries around the world.

The Academy Scholars Program was established to support outstanding researchers at the beginning of their academic careers whose work combines:

  • Excellence in a social science discipline
  • Strong regional or country expertise
  • Knowledge of languages relevant to their research where appropriate
  • Original and innovative research
  • Comparative, transnational or domestic research questions
  • The potential to develop a successful career in a research university or international institution

The programme is particularly interested in scholars whose research connects disciplinary expertise with knowledge of regions outside the United States and Canada.

What Is the Harvard Academy Scholars Program?

The Academy Scholars Program is a two-year, in-residence postdoctoral fellowship at Harvard University in Cambridge, Massachusetts.

Each year, approximately five to six scholars are selected for two-year appointments. Selected scholars receive an annual stipend of US$80,000, in addition to US$6,000 in annual research support.

The fellowship provides scholars with the time and resources necessary to undertake substantial research, writing and professional development during the early stages of their academic careers.

Academy Scholars become part of a select interdisciplinary community and participate in academic activities with other scholars and Harvard faculty members.

The programme also provides opportunities for scholars to interact with the Harvard Academy’s Senior Scholars, who serve as mentors and members of the selection committee.

Harvard Academy Scholars Program 2027–2028 Benefits

The fellowship provides several important benefits designed to support scholars during their two-year appointment.

1. Annual Stipend of US$80,000

Each Academy Scholar receives an annual stipend of US$80,000.

This substantial financial support allows fellows to dedicate significant time to research, writing and academic development without the financial pressures that can accompany early-career research.

2. Annual Research Support of US$6,000

In addition to the annual stipend, Academy Scholars receive US$6,000 per year in research support.

This funding can help facilitate research-related activities associated with the scholar’s approved academic work.

3. Two-Year Fellowship

The appointment is structured as a two-year postdoctoral fellowship.

The fellowship provides an extended period for scholars to develop their research programmes, publish academic work and establish themselves as independent researchers.

The Academy notes that the two years must be completed within a three-year window.

4. Research and Writing Opportunities

The programme is specifically designed to provide scholars with time to undertake significant research and writing.

Scholars may use the fellowship period to develop work based on their doctoral research, prepare a dissertation for publication or begin a new research project.

5. Mentorship

Academy Scholars are mentored by the Harvard Academy’s Senior Scholars.

These faculty members participate in Academy activities and support fellows as they develop their research and academic careers.

6. Interdisciplinary Academic Community

Academy Scholars participate in dinners, seminars and informal academic gatherings.

These activities encourage scholars from different disciplines and regional specializations to exchange ideas and develop interdisciplinary approaches to research.

7. Harvard University Research Environment

Being based at Harvard University provides Academy Scholars with access to a major international academic environment and opportunities to interact with researchers, faculty and other scholars.

The programme is particularly suited to researchers who would benefit from an intellectually intensive period dedicated to research and publication.

Who Is Eligible for the Harvard Academy Scholars Program 2027–2028?

The Academy Scholars Program is open to scholars from all countries and citizenships.

However, applicants must meet specific doctoral and disciplinary requirements.

The programme is intended for scholars who have recently completed or are nearing completion of a PhD or equivalent degree in the social sciences. Equivalent degrees include programmes such as the DPhil and SJD where applicable.

Applicants Who Have Already Completed Their PhD

If you have completed your PhD, your degree must have been completed within two years of the fellowship’s August 1, 2027 start date.

For the September 18, 2026 application deadline, applicants who have already completed their PhD must have completed it on or after August 1, 2025.

Current PhD Candidates

Applicants who are still completing their doctoral degree may also apply.

However, they must be sufficiently advanced in their programme and able to provide official degree-conferral documentation from their university registrar by June 30, 2027.

This requirement is important because successful applicants must be able to begin the fellowship on the required schedule.

Applicants Who Have Previously Held a Postdoctoral Fellowship

Individuals who hold or have completed another postdoctoral fellowship are not eligible to apply.

Applicants should therefore carefully consider their previous postdoctoral experience before submitting an application.

Eligible Fields of Study

The Harvard Academy does not accept applications from every academic discipline.

The programme focuses on the social sciences, particularly research that examines regions and countries outside the United States and Canada.

Eligible social science fields include:

  • Anthropology
  • Economics
  • Ethnic Studies
  • Geography
  • Government
  • History
  • History of Science
  • International Relations
  • Law
  • Political Economy and Government
  • Political Science
  • Psychology
  • Public Policy
  • Social Policy
  • Social Studies
  • Sociology
  • Women, Gender, and Sexuality

Applicants from regional studies disciplines may also be considered when their research is clearly grounded in one or more of the accepted social science disciplines.

Regional Studies Fields That May Be Eligible

The Academy welcomes applicants from several regional studies fields when the research is appropriately designed around the accepted social science disciplines.

These include:

  • African Studies
  • Asian Studies
  • Central Asian Studies
  • East Asian Languages and Civilizations
  • Eastern European Studies
  • Inner Asian and Altaic Studies
  • Latin American and Iberian Studies
  • Middle East Studies
  • Near Eastern Languages and Civilizations
  • Russia Studies
  • Slavic Languages and Civilization
  • South Asian Studies
  • Southeast Asian Studies
  • Ukraine Studies
  • Western European Studies

The key consideration is not simply the name of the degree programme. The applicant’s research must clearly engage with one or more of the Academy’s eligible social science disciplines.

Fields That Are Not Accepted

The Harvard Academy also identifies a number of areas that are not eligible.

The list includes:

  • Research focused on the United States or Canada
  • Archaeology
  • Architecture
  • Art History
  • Business
  • Classics
  • Global Health
  • Linguistics
  • Literature
  • Management
  • Medieval Studies
  • Musicology
  • Philosophy
  • Public Administration
  • Religion
  • Sanskrit and Indian Studies
  • Social Work
  • Urban Studies

The Academy notes that this list is not exhaustive.

Applicants should therefore carefully compare their doctoral field and research focus with the official eligibility criteria before applying.

A Major Requirement: Research Must Focus Outside the United States or Canada

Applicants should pay close attention to the Academy’s regional focus.

The programme seeks scholars whose work combines social science expertise with knowledge of countries or regions outside the United States or Canada.

Therefore, an otherwise eligible scholar may not qualify if the proposed research is primarily focused on the United States or Canada.

This regional requirement is central to the intellectual purpose of the programme and distinguishes the Academy Scholars Program from many other postdoctoral fellowships.

Harvard Academy Scholars Program Application Requirements

Applicants must submit a complete online application containing several important documents.

1. Curriculum Vitae

Applicants must submit a CV that includes their academic and professional background as well as a list of publications.

The CV should provide a clear overview of the applicant’s:

  • Academic qualifications
  • Research experience
  • Publications
  • Awards and recognitions
  • Teaching experience where applicable
  • Fellowships
  • Professional appointments
  • Relevant academic activities

2. Research Proposal

Applicants must submit a research proposal of no more than 2,000 words.

The proposal should explain the intellectual objectives of the research and the methodological and disciplinary work the applicant plans to undertake.

The Academy’s selection committee is particularly interested in:

  • The relevance of the proposed research
  • Its contribution to the applicant’s discipline
  • The originality of the research
  • The researcher’s plans for the two-year fellowship
  • Future publication plans
  • Future research plans

References and citations do not count toward the 2,000-word limit.

3. Scholarly Writing Sample

Applicants must submit one scholarly writing sample.

Examples include:

  • A chapter from a PhD dissertation
  • A peer-reviewed academic journal article
  • Another substantial scholarly work

The writing sample must:

  • Be written in English
  • Be no longer than 50 pages
  • Represent approximately the length of a single PhD dissertation chapter or academic journal article
  • Be submitted as one sample only

A published or unpublished work may be used.

Co-authored work is permitted provided that the applicant’s contribution is clearly identified and the work is not co-authored with an academic adviser.

4. PhD Program Transcript

Applicants must submit a copy of their PhD programme transcript.

For applicants who studied at universities outside the United States, the Academy advises that applicants provide as much official transcript-like documentation as their university registrar can provide for their graduate studies, including relevant Master’s and PhD records.

5. Three Letters of Recommendation

Applicants must provide three letters of recommendation.

The letters must be uploaded directly and confidentially by the recommenders through the online application system.

Importantly, applicants must first submit their application before the recommendation upload link is sent to the recommenders.

This means applicants should contact their potential recommenders well in advance of the deadline.

The recommendation letters have a later submission deadline than the main application materials: they must arrive no later than September 28, 2026, at 11:59 PM EDT.

Learn More HERE!

Application Deadline for the 2027–2028 Harvard Academy Scholars Program

The main application deadline is:

September 18, 2026, at 11:59 PM EDT.

Harvard Academy states that late applications are not accepted.

All application materials other than the recommendation letters must be received by this deadline.

Recommendation letters must arrive by:

September 28, 2026, at 11:59 PM EDT.

Applicants should therefore not wait until the final day to begin or submit their application.

APPLY HERE

Important 2027–2028 Application Timeline

Key dates include:

  • September 18, 2026, 11:59 PM EDT: Main application deadline
  • September 28, 2026, 11:59 PM EDT: Deadline for recommendation letters
  • December 4, 2026: Interview date for finalists
  • December 2026: Expected announcement of awards
  • June 30, 2027: Deadline for doctoral candidates to provide degree-conferral documentation
  • August 1, 2027: Fellowship start date

Finalists must be available for the personal interview scheduled for December 4, 2026. The Harvard Academy will make arrangements for finalists to participate in the interview.

Where Is the Fellowship Located?

The Harvard Academy Scholars Program is based at Harvard University in Cambridge, Massachusetts, United States.

The Harvard Academy for International and Area Studies is located within the Weatherhead Center for International Affairs at:

1727 Cambridge Street
Cambridge, MA 02138
USA

The fellowship is an in-residence programme, meaning Academy Scholars are expected to participate actively in the Harvard academic community during the formal programming period.

Residency and Fieldwork Requirements

Academy Scholars are expected to be in residence and participate fully in the scholarly community during the formal programming period, which runs approximately from late August through the end of April.

Scholars can conduct extensive fieldwork during the winter, spring and summer breaks.

Short trips for conferences and other academic engagements may be permitted provided that they do not interfere with Harvard Academy obligations.

This requirement is important for applicants whose research involves extensive international fieldwork.

The fellowship is designed around participation in an active academic community at Harvard rather than being a fully remote research fellowship.

Can the Fellowship Start Date Be Deferred?

No.

Successful applicants cannot postpone or defer the August 1, 2027 start date.

Year 1 must begin no later than the fall immediately following the fellowship offer.

The two fellowship years must also be completed within the programme’s specified three-year window.

Applicants should therefore apply only if they will be able to commit to the required timeline.

How Competitive Is the Harvard Academy Scholars Program?

The Academy Scholars Program is extremely competitive.

The Harvard Academy states that it receives more than 500 applications in many years but typically selects only five or six scholars.

Historical statistics demonstrate the selectivity of the programme. For example:

  • Fall 2016: 716 completed applications, 4 selected
  • Fall 2019: 585 completed applications, 5 selected
  • Fall 2022: 350 completed applications, 5 selected
  • Fall 2024: 533 completed applications, 6 selected
  • Fall 2025: 522 completed applications, 5 selected

These figures demonstrate why applicants need to present a highly focused research agenda and compelling evidence of scholarly potential.

How to Prepare a Strong Harvard Academy Application

Because the programme is highly selective, applicants should approach the application strategically.

1. Develop a Clear Research Question

Your research proposal should communicate exactly what problem you intend to investigate.

Avoid presenting a broad topic without a clear research question.

Explain:

  • What you want to study
  • Why the question matters
  • What is already known
  • What gap your research addresses
  • What contribution you intend to make
  • How you will conduct the research

2. Demonstrate Disciplinary Contribution

The Academy specifically emphasizes the relevance and contribution of the proposed research to the applicant’s discipline.

Your proposal should therefore make the academic contribution explicit rather than assuming that the committee will infer it.

3. Explain Your Two-Year Research Plan

Applicants should explain how they intend to use the fellowship period.

For example, a scholar may use the first year to develop doctoral research into a book or series of articles and use the second year to begin a new research project.

If you plan to move in a new research direction, explain how the new project connects with or expands upon your doctoral research.

4. Select Your Writing Sample Carefully

The writing sample is an important demonstration of your scholarly ability.

Choose one piece that clearly demonstrates:

  • Strong argumentation
  • Original thinking
  • Research competence
  • Evidence-based analysis
  • Clear academic writing
  • Strong methodological reasoning where relevant

Do not submit multiple writing samples because the Academy specifically requests only one.

5. Contact Recommenders Early

Since recommendation letters must be submitted separately, applicants should contact their recommenders well before the application deadline.

Waiting until the final days can create unnecessary risks, especially if a recommender is unavailable or encounters technical difficulties.

6. Check Your Regional Fit

One of the most important elements of the Academy Scholars Program is its focus on regions outside the United States and Canada.

Applicants should clearly demonstrate how their research engages with a specific country, region or broader comparative question that fits the Academy’s mission.

Learn More HERE

Why This Fellowship Is Valuable for Early-Career Researchers

The transition from completing a PhD to establishing an independent academic career can be challenging.

Researchers often need time to transform doctoral research into publications while developing new research projects and establishing an independent scholarly identity.

The Harvard Academy Scholars Program addresses this need by providing:

  • A two-year research environment
  • A substantial annual stipend
  • Dedicated research funding
  • Mentorship
  • An interdisciplinary scholarly community
  • Opportunities for academic exchange
  • Time to develop publications
  • Access to the Harvard academic environment

The programme is particularly valuable for researchers whose work sits at the intersection of social science discipline and regional expertise.

Important Advice for International Applicants

International applicants are explicitly welcome, regardless of citizenship or where they completed their graduate studies.

However, applicants studying outside the United States should ensure that their academic documentation is sufficiently detailed.

The Academy advises international applicants to obtain official transcript-like documentation for their graduate studies from their university registrar where necessary.

Applicants should also consider the practical implications of an in-residence fellowship in Cambridge, Massachusetts, including the requirement to participate in the programme’s formal activities.

Who Should Consider Applying?

The Harvard Academy Scholars Program may be particularly suitable for an applicant who:

  • Has recently completed a PhD in an eligible social science field
  • Is an advanced doctoral candidate nearing completion
  • Has a strong academic record
  • Has a clearly defined research agenda
  • Conducts research focused on a region outside the United States or Canada
  • Has demonstrated scholarly potential
  • Has strong writing and research experience
  • Wants to develop doctoral research into publications
  • Is planning an independent research project
  • Can commit to a two-year in-residence fellowship
  • Has not previously completed a postdoctoral fellowship

Researchers from Africa, Asia, Europe, Latin America, the Middle East and other regions may apply because the programme accepts scholars of all nationalities, provided they satisfy the academic and research requirements.

How to Apply for the Harvard Academy Scholars Program

Applications are submitted online through the Harvard Academy’s application system.

Applicants should prepare the required documents before beginning the submission process:

  1. Curriculum vitae with publication list
  2. Research proposal of no more than 2,000 words
  3. One English-language scholarly writing sample of no more than 50 pages
  4. PhD programme transcript
  5. Three confidential letters of recommendation

All application materials are submitted online as PDF documents.

The application should be completed and submitted by September 18, 2026, at 11:59 PM EDT, while recommendation letters must arrive by September 28, 2026, at 11:59 PM EDT.

Applicants can access the application through the official Harvard Academy website.

Official Harvard Academy Scholars Program:
Visit the Harvard Academy Scholars Program page

Online Application:
Apply through Harvard’s online application portal

Frequently Asked Questions

Is the Harvard Academy Scholars Program fully funded?

The programme provides substantial financial support, including an annual US$80,000 stipend and US$6,000 annual research support. It is therefore a highly funded postdoctoral fellowship, although applicants should review the official terms carefully rather than assuming that every possible personal expense is covered.

Can applicants from Africa apply?

Yes. The Academy states that the programme is open to scholars from all countries and citizenships. African applicants are eligible provided they meet the doctoral, disciplinary, regional and other programme requirements.

Can current PhD students apply?

Yes. Advanced doctoral candidates can apply if they will be able to submit official degree-conferral documentation from their university registrar by June 30, 2027.

Can someone with a PhD apply?

Yes, provided the PhD was completed within two years of the August 1, 2027 start date. For the current application cycle, the PhD must have been completed on or after August 1, 2025.

Can someone who has already completed another postdoctoral fellowship apply?

No. Individuals who hold or have completed another postdoctoral fellowship are not eligible.

Is there an age limit?

The official eligibility information focuses on the timing of PhD completion or expected completion rather than specifying a general age limit. Applicants should therefore assess eligibility primarily according to their doctoral status and completion date.

Can the fellowship be deferred?

No. The August 1, 2027 start date cannot be postponed or deferred.

Can Academy Scholars conduct research outside Cambridge?

Yes, but extensive fieldwork should generally be scheduled during winter, spring or summer breaks. Scholars are expected to remain in residence and participate in the Academy’s formal programming during the main academic period.

How many scholars are selected?

The Academy generally selects approximately five to six scholars each year, although the exact number can vary.

Conclusion

The Harvard Academy Scholars Program 2027–2028 represents a highly competitive opportunity for emerging social scientists seeking dedicated time, financial support and an exceptional academic environment to advance their research.

The two-year in-residence postdoctoral fellowship at Harvard University provides selected scholars with an US$80,000 annual stipend, US$6,000 in annual research support, mentorship from Senior Scholars and opportunities to participate in an interdisciplinary scholarly community.

The programme is open to applicants from all countries and citizenships, making it accessible to qualified researchers worldwide. However, applicants must meet the programme’s strict academic requirements, including having recently completed or being close to completing a PhD or equivalent degree in an eligible social science field. Their research must also demonstrate meaningful expertise in countries or regions outside the United States or Canada.

Because only a small number of Academy Scholars are selected each year, prospective applicants should invest considerable time in developing a compelling research proposal, selecting a strong scholarly writing sample, preparing an academic CV and securing high-quality recommendation letters.

For the 2027–2028 cohort, the main application deadline is September 18, 2026, at 11:59 PM EDT, while recommendation letters must arrive by September 28, 2026, at 11:59 PM EDT.

Eligible researchers should begin preparing their applications well in advance and carefully review the official Harvard Academy requirements before submitting. This is particularly important for international and regional studies applicants, as the programme’s disciplinary and geographic focus is central to the selection process.
