item.content:encoded:
The NextGen@ICANN88 Programme 2026 is inviting eligible young students to apply for an opportunity to participate in the global Internet governance community through the Internet Corporation for Assigned Names and Numbers (ICANN).

The programme is designed for young people who are interested in Internet governance, the future of the Internet, digital policy, technology and other issues addressed within the ICANN ecosystem. Selected participants will receive coaching, guidance and travel support to attend an ICANN meeting, giving them an opportunity to learn directly from experts, engage with the international ICANN community and begin building a pathway toward long-term participation in Internet governance.

For the current application round, the programme is associated with the ICANN88 Community Forum, which will take place in Lisbon, Portugal, from 13–18 March 2027. Applications are open from 31 August 2026 until 9 October 2026 at 23:59 UTC.

What Is the NextGen@ICANN Programme?

The NextGen@ICANN Programme is a youth-focused initiative established to encourage greater participation by young people in ICANN and the wider Internet governance ecosystem.

ICANN recognizes that the future of the Internet depends not only on established experts and institutions, but also on bringing new generations of people into discussions about how the global Internet operates and evolves. The NextGen@ICANN Programme therefore seeks to identify young people who have the potential to become future contributors to the ICANN community.

The programme introduces participants to important areas of ICANN’s work while helping them understand the bottom-up, multistakeholder model used in Internet governance. Participants can learn how different stakeholders contribute to discussions and decision-making processes that affect the Internet at regional and global levels.

For students interested in technology, digital transformation, cybersecurity, Internet policy, communications, governance, law, computer science, public policy or related areas, the programme can provide an opportunity to gain exposure to an international environment where important conversations about the Internet take place.

Why Consider NextGen@ICANN88?

Participating in NextGen@ICANN can provide more than attendance at an international conference. The programme is structured to help young participants understand the ICANN ecosystem and gradually become involved in the wider Internet governance community.

Selected participants receive coaching and guidance, as well as financial support associated with attending the relevant ICANN meeting. This makes the programme particularly valuable for students who want international exposure but may otherwise find it difficult to attend a major global meeting independently.

ICANN describes participation in a NextGen@ICANN meeting as an ideal first step for young people beginning their journey into the ICANN ecosystem. Participants are expected not simply to attend but to engage meaningfully with the programme and meeting activities.

Some of the potential benefits include:

  • International exposure: Participants can interact with members of an international Internet governance community.
  • Coaching and guidance: Selected students receive support intended to help them understand ICANN and its broader ecosystem.
  • Travel support: The programme provides financial support toward attending the ICANN meeting.
  • Economy-class airfare: The support grant covers the cost of economy-class airfare.
  • Hotel accommodation: Selected participants receive support for hotel costs associated with participation.
  • Stipend: Participants are provided with a stipend as part of the programme’s support package.
  • Internet governance knowledge: Participants gain a deeper understanding of Internet governance and issues discussed within the ICANN community.
  • Networking opportunities: The programme can introduce young students to people working and participating in different areas of the global Internet ecosystem.
  • Opportunity to present a project: Selected participants are required to prepare and deliver a 5–10-minute presentation at the meeting.
  • Potential long-term engagement: The programme is intended to encourage young people to become future members and contributors to the ICANN community.

What Is the ICANN88 Community Forum?

The current NextGen application round is for ICANN88, the Community Forum scheduled to take place in Lisbon, Portugal, from 13 to 18 March 2027.

ICANN meetings rotate among different geographic regions. The ICANN88 meeting falls within the Europe region. According to the programme’s eligibility requirements, applicants generally need to be living and studying in the region of the respective ICANN meeting.
This means that students interested in applying for the current ICANN88 NextGen opportunity should carefully verify that they meet the geographic requirement for the Europe-based meeting.

Who Can Apply for NextGen@ICANN88?

The NextGen@ICANN Programme has specific eligibility requirements. Applicants should carefully review these conditions before beginning an application.

1. Applicants Must Be Students

Applicants must be currently enrolled as an undergraduate, graduate or doctoral student.

This means the programme is intended for people who are actively pursuing higher education rather than applicants who have already completed their studies and are no longer enrolled.

Eligible study levels include:

  • Undergraduate students
  • Graduate students
  • Doctoral students

The source does not limit eligibility to a single academic discipline. Therefore, applicants should focus on demonstrating how their studies, research, activities or interests connect with Internet governance, the future of the Internet or subjects relevant to ICANN.

2. Applicants Must Be Between 18 and 30 Years Old

Applicants must be between 18 and 30 years of age at the time of the ICANN meeting.

For ICANN88, the relevant meeting takes place in March 2027, so applicants should ensure that they satisfy the age requirement at the time the meeting occurs, rather than looking only at their age on the application date.

3. Applicants Must Live and Study in the Relevant Region

A major requirement is that applicants must be currently living and studying in the region of the respective ICANN meeting.

ICANN rotates its meetings through five geographic regions:

  1. Africa
  2. Europe
  3. North America
  4. Latin America
  5. Asia Pacific

For the current NextGen@ICANN88 application, the meeting is scheduled for Lisbon, Portugal, in the Europe region. Consequently, the regional eligibility requirement is particularly important for applicants considering this round.

ICANN also notes that if applications are accepted from regions other than the region in which a particular meeting is taking place, that information will be made publicly available before applications open for that meeting.

4. Applicants Should Have an Interest in Internet Governance

Applicants should demonstrate an interest in Internet governance, the future of the Internet and other topics covered at ICANN meetings.

This is important because the programme is not simply a general international travel opportunity for students. Applicants are expected to have a genuine interest in the issues addressed by ICANN and the Internet governance ecosystem.

An applicant can therefore strengthen their application by clearly explaining their connection to Internet-related issues through their studies, research, projects, professional activities, public discussions or other relevant engagements.

What Will Selected Participants Be Expected to Do?

Being selected for NextGen@ICANN comes with active participation requirements.

Participants are expected to attend the relevant ICANN meeting and required events and to participate actively throughout the programme. The opportunity is therefore best suited to students who are genuinely interested in learning, engaging and contributing rather than simply attending the event as observers.

Participants Must Present a Project

One of the notable requirements is that selected participants must be willing to deliver a 5–10-minute project presentation at the meeting.

The presentation can focus on different types of work, including

  • Research the applicant is currently working on
  • Research the applicant has already completed
  • An activity connected to ICANN’s work
  • An ICANN-related website with which the applicant is affiliated
  • A thesis project
  • Another relevant project connected to the programme’s themes

This requirement provides applicants with an opportunity to demonstrate their knowledge, interests and ability to communicate an Internet-related subject to an international audience.

Applicants should therefore think carefully about the project they could present if selected.

What Financial Support Does NextGen@ICANN Provide?

One of the major attractions of the programme is the financial support available to selected participants.

Each selected participant receives a grant of support covering:

  • Economy-class airfare
  • Hotel accommodation
  • A stipend

This support is designed to enable selected students to attend the ICANN meeting and participate in the required programme activities.

However, applicants should be aware that the support does not cover every travel-related expense.

Visa Costs

Participants are responsible for securing their own visas for travel, and the cost of obtaining the visa is at the participant’s own expense.

Applicants should therefore investigate visa requirements well in advance if they are selected, particularly because international travel arrangements may require additional documentation and processing time.

Travel and Health Insurance

If a participant wishes to obtain travel insurance or health insurance, those costs are also the participant’s responsibility.

Applicants should take this into consideration when planning for participation.

How Are NextGen@ICANN Applicants Selected?

Meeting the basic eligibility requirements does not automatically guarantee selection.

ICANN evaluates applications using a number of selection criteria designed to identify applicants who demonstrate genuine interest in Internet governance and the potential to contribute to the community.

The selection criteria include:

Demonstrated Interest in ICANN and the Internet Ecosystem

Applicants should demonstrate their interest in ICANN and the broader Internet ecosystem through examples of their current work, activities, studies, research or public dialogue on the web.

This means applicants should not simply state that they are interested in Internet governance. They should provide evidence that supports that interest.

Value of Participation to the Applicant and Their Community

Applicants are assessed on how clearly they explain the value that participating in NextGen@ICANN would provide to them personally and to a wider community.

The wider community could include a:

  • University
  • Country
  • Region
  • Other relevant community

Applicants should therefore consider not only what they hope to gain, but also how they could use the experience and knowledge gained through participation to benefit others.

Quality of the Applicant’s View on an Internet Topic

The application also considers the applicant’s ability to express their views on an Internet-related topic.

This makes the quality of written responses particularly important. Applicants should aim to communicate their ideas clearly, demonstrate genuine understanding and present thoughtful perspectives on relevant Internet issues.

Desire to Join the ICANN Community

Applicants should demonstrate that they genuinely want to become part of the ICANN community.

The programme is intended to support future engagement, so applicants who can clearly explain their interest in continuing to participate in Internet governance may be better positioned to demonstrate alignment with the programme’s objectives.

Long-Term Interest in ICANN-Related Topics

ICANN also considers whether an applicant has demonstrated a long-standing interest in topics related to ICANN’s work.

Applicants should therefore consider how their academic background, research, projects, professional interests or other activities demonstrate sustained engagement with Internet-related subjects.

Desire to Understand and Engage With Regional ICANN Work

Applicants are also assessed on their desire to engage with and improve their understanding of ICANN’s work in their region.

This reinforces the importance of explaining why participation is relevant not only to the applicant personally but also to the Internet governance environment in their region.

How to Prepare a Strong NextGen@ICANN Application

Although selection is competitive, applicants can take practical steps to make their applications stronger.

Demonstrate Genuine Interest

Avoid relying on generic statements about loving technology or wanting international exposure. Instead, connect your experience to specific Internet governance issues.

For example, an applicant could discuss relevant:

  • Academic research
  • University projects
  • Digital policy activities
  • Internet-related initiatives
  • Research publications
  • Technology projects
  • Online discussions
  • Community activities
  • Thesis work
  • Professional activities related to Internet governance

The objective should be to show evidence of genuine engagement rather than simply claiming interest.

Explain the Impact of Participation

Applicants should clearly explain why NextGen@ICANN matters to their personal development and how participation could benefit their university, country or region.

A strong response should make a clear connection between:

Current experience → ICANN opportunity → knowledge gained → future contribution.

This can help demonstrate alignment with the programme’s objective of developing future members of the ICANN community.

Prepare a Relevant Project

Because selected participants are expected to present a project for 5–10 minutes, applicants should consider what work they could potentially showcase.

A thesis, research project, Internet-related initiative, relevant website or other activity may provide a suitable foundation for the presentation.

Demonstrate Your Regional Perspective

Since eligibility and participation are linked to ICANN’s geographic regions, applicants should consider how Internet governance issues affect their own region.

Explaining a regional Internet challenge, policy issue, digital inclusion question, cybersecurity concern or other relevant subject may help demonstrate the applicant’s understanding of the broader Internet ecosystem.

Application Requirements and ICANN Account

Applicants should be aware that an ICANN Account is required to apply for the NextGen@ICANN Programme.

The application is submitted through ICANN’s application platform, and prospective applicants should make sure they have the necessary account access before attempting to submit their application.

Applicants can access the official application route through the NextGen@ICANN programme page and should follow ICANN’s instructions for the relevant application round.

NextGen@ICANN88 Application Deadline

The NextGen@ICANN88 application period opened on 31 August 2026 and closes on 9 October 2026 at 23:59 UTC.

This is the key deadline prospective applicants should keep in mind.

The selection announcement for ICANN88 is scheduled for 17 December 2026.

Important Dates at a Glance

  • Application opening date: 31 August 2026
  • Application deadline: 9 October 2026 at 23:59 UTC
  • Selection announcement: 17 December 2026
  • ICANN88 Community Forum: 13–18 March 2027
  • Location: Lisbon, Portugal
  • ICANN region: Europe

Applicants should avoid waiting until the final day to submit their applications. Creating an ICANN Account, reviewing eligibility, preparing application responses and identifying a suitable project for presentation can all take time.

APPLY HERE

Geographic Eligibility: Which Countries Can Apply?

The programme’s eligibility is based primarily on ICANN geographic regions, rather than a simple worldwide open application model.

ICANN identifies five meeting regions:

  • Africa
  • Europe
  • North America
  • Latin America
  • Asia Pacific

Applicants are generally expected to be living and studying in the region of the respective ICANN meeting.

For ICANN88, the meeting is scheduled in Lisbon, Portugal, and the listed region is Europe. Therefore, the current application round is aimed at eligible students living and studying in the Europe region, subject to any specific announcement by ICANN concerning applications from other regions.

The source does not provide a country-by-country list of eligible countries for ICANN88, so applicants should use ICANN’s official regional classification rather than assuming that every country is eligible based solely on geographical proximity.

There is also no race-based restriction stated in the eligibility information provided. The requirements focus on age, student status, residence and study location, interest in Internet governance, ability to attend and willingness to participate and present a project.

What Makes NextGen@ICANN Different?

Many international opportunities provide students with funding or access to events, but NextGen@ICANN places significant emphasis on participation and long-term engagement.

The programme is designed to help young people understand the Internet governance ecosystem and progressively become involved in the ICANN community.

This makes it particularly relevant to students who want to develop expertise in areas where technology intersects with policy, governance and international cooperation.

The opportunity can be especially valuable for students interested in fields such as

  • Internet governance
  • Digital policy
  • Technology policy
  • Information and communication technologies
  • Computer science
  • Cybersecurity
  • Law and technology
  • Public policy
  • Digital rights
  • Internet infrastructure
  • Communications
  • Digital development
  • Technology governance
  • International relations
  • Research involving the Internet ecosystem

The programme itself does not restrict applicants to these fields in the eligibility information provided, so applicants should focus on demonstrating their genuine connection to ICANN-related topics.

Frequently Asked Questions About NextGen@ICANN88

Is NextGen@ICANN a scholarship?

No. It is not a traditional academic scholarship. It is a youth participation and development programme that provides selected students with coaching, guidance and financial support to attend an ICANN meeting.

The support includes economy-class airfare, hotel accommodation and a stipend.

Do applicants have to be university students?

Yes. Applicants must be enrolled as an undergraduate, graduate or doctoral student.

What is the age requirement?

Applicants must be between 18 and 30 years old at the time of the ICANN meeting.

Can applicants from any country apply?

Not necessarily. Eligibility is linked to the region of the ICANN meeting. For ICANN88, the meeting is in Lisbon, Portugal, within the Europe region, and applicants are expected to be living and studying in the relevant region.

Does ICANN cover airfare?

Yes. Selected participants receive a support grant covering economy-class airfare.

Does ICANN provide accommodation?

Yes. The support grant covers hotel accommodation for selected participants.

Is a stipend provided?

Yes. The NextGen@ICANN support package includes a stipend.

Does ICANN pay for visas?

No. Participants must secure their own visas and pay the associated costs themselves.

Are participants required to present?

Yes. Selected participants must be willing to present a project lasting 5–10 minutes during the meeting.

When does the ICANN88 application close?

The application closes on 9 October 2026 at 23:59 UTC.

Conclusion

The NextGen@ICANN88 Programme 2026 offers eligible young students an opportunity to move beyond simply studying technology and become more actively involved in conversations about the future of the Internet.

Through coaching, guidance, travel support, accommodation and a stipend, selected participants can attend the ICANN88 Community Forum in Lisbon and engage directly with the international Internet governance ecosystem. The programme also provides participants with an opportunity to present their own research or project and begin developing a longer-term relationship with the ICANN community.
The opportunity is particularly relevant for students who are 18–30 years old, currently enrolled in undergraduate, graduate or doctoral studies, living and studying in the relevant ICANN meeting region, and genuinely interested in Internet governance and the future of the Internet.

For the current ICANN88 round, eligible applicants should take note of the 9 October 2026 at 23:59 UTC deadline and prepare their applications carefully. Beyond meeting the basic eligibility requirements, applicants should demonstrate their existing interest in ICANN and Internet-related issues, explain how participation would benefit them and their wider community, and show their potential to become an engaged member of the ICANN ecosystem.

For young students seeking international exposure, knowledge, networking and a structured introduction to global Internet governance, NextGen@ICANN88 represents a valuable opportunity to learn, participate and contribute to discussions shaping the future of the Internet.

item.content:encoded:
United Airlines is currently offering a wide range of student and early career job opportunities, including internships, co-op positions and other entry-level roles for students and emerging professionals looking to build careers in the aviation industry.

The airline’s Student and Early Career Jobs portal currently features 45 opportunities across areas including Corporate, Digital Technology, Technical Operations, Airport operations, Customer Solutions, Flight Attendant roles and other career pathways.

Among the opportunities currently listed are several Summer 2027 internships in Chicago, Illinois, covering technical operations, engineering, procurement, inflight operations, corporate safety, sales, pricing, revenue management and cargo operations.

For students and recent graduates interested in aviation, business, technology, engineering, finance, supply chain, analytics and related fields, these opportunities provide a chance to gain practical experience with one of the world’s major airlines.

About United Airlines Student and Early Career Opportunities

United Airlines has established dedicated career pathways for students and early-career professionals. The company’s student and early-career platform is designed for individuals who are approaching graduation, exploring their first professional opportunities or looking to gain practical experience through internships and co-op programmes.

United states that its student and early-career opportunities provide participants with opportunities to work on projects that contribute to the company’s operations while developing professional skills and connections.

The company’s student programmes can include:

  • Internships
  • Co-op opportunities
  • Early-career positions
  • Digital technology programmes
  • Technical operations opportunities
  • Corporate roles
  • Commercial opportunities
  • Finance-related positions
  • Aviation and operational career pathways

United also highlights mentorship, hands-on learning, networking and customized intern programming as part of the student and early-career experience.

United Airlines Summer 2027 Internship Opportunities

The current listings include multiple internships scheduled for Summer 2027. Several of the opportunities listed on the supplied careers page are based in Chicago, Illinois, United States.

The positions currently highlighted include the following:

1. Intern – Tech Ops Strategy & Performance

Location: Chicago, Illinois, United States

This internship is within United’s Technical Operations organization. Interns will support analytical projects and collaborate with cross-functional teams working to improve maintenance strategies and operational performance.

The position is particularly relevant to students interested in:

  • Aviation operations
  • Technical operations
  • Business analytics
  • Strategy
  • Engineering
  • Maintenance planning

The listing indicates that it is suited to rising sophomores pursuing a relevant degree and interested in aviation operations.

2. Intern – Facilities & GSE Maintenance

Location: Chicago, Illinois, United States

This internship focuses on United’s Facilities and Ground Support Equipment Maintenance operations.

Interns can gain practical exposure to operational challenges and engineering projects while working alongside experienced professionals.

The position is particularly relevant to students studying:

  • Mechanical Engineering
  • Civil Engineering
  • Electrical Engineering
  • Industrial Engineering
  • Related engineering disciplines

This opportunity can be valuable for students seeking practical engineering experience within the aviation industry.

3. Masters/MBA Intern – Global Procurement

Location: Chicago, Illinois, United States

United is also recruiting for a Masters/MBA Global Procurement Intern for Summer 2027.

The position focuses on areas such as:

  • Global procurement
  • Operational improvement
  • Automation
  • Process enhancement
  • Supply chain
  • Finance
  • Business operations

The listing indicates that candidates with prior work experience and academic backgrounds in finance, supply chain or related disciplines may be particularly suitable.

This position may therefore be especially attractive to graduate students and MBA candidates seeking to apply their academic knowledge to a large-scale international airline environment.

4. Intern – Inflight Entertainment

Location: Chicago, Illinois, United States

This role provides an opportunity to work in an area connected to United’s inflight customer experience and catering operations.

The position involves supporting projects designed to maintain high operational and food-safety standards while contributing to data analysis and customer-focused initiatives.

It may be suitable for early-career candidates with interests or academic backgrounds in:

  • Engineering
  • Business
  • Food Science
  • Data analysis
  • Operations
  • Customer experience

5. Intern – Corporate Safety

Location: Chicago, Illinois, United States

United’s Corporate Safety internship focuses on supporting safety-related projects and initiatives.

Interns may contribute to:

  • Safety risk assessments
  • Data analytics
  • Business intelligence
  • Operations safety projects
  • Risk management

This role can be particularly relevant to students interested in aviation safety, analytics, engineering, business intelligence, risk management and operational management.

6. Intern – Sales Pricing & Strategy

Location: Chicago, Illinois, United States

The Sales Pricing & Strategy internship provides students with exposure to United’s commercial operations.

Interns will support United’s Worldwide Sales organization through data-driven analysis and strategic projects.

Potential areas of experience include:

  • Sales strategy
  • Pricing
  • Business analytics
  • Commercial strategy
  • Data analysis
  • Communication
  • Revenue-related decision-making

Students pursuing relevant degrees with strong analytical and communication skills may find this opportunity particularly suitable.

7. Intern – Tech Ops Strategic Planning

Location: Chicago, Illinois, United States

This Technical Operations internship focuses on strategic planning and operational projects within United’s aviation maintenance organization.

The role can provide exposure to areas such as:

  • Data analytics
  • Fleet management
  • Maintenance planning
  • Technical operations
  • Strategic planning
  • Aviation engineering

It is particularly relevant to students studying engineering, business or related disciplines who want hands-on experience in airline operations.

8. Intern – Pricing & Revenue Management

Location: Chicago, Illinois, United States

United is also recruiting a Pricing & Revenue Management Intern for Summer 2027.

The role focuses on projects that contribute to revenue growth and commercial decision-making.

Students may gain experience in:

  • Pricing strategy
  • Revenue management
  • Demand forecasting
  • Data analysis
  • Commercial strategy
  • Cross-functional collaboration

The listing indicates that this role is suitable for undergraduate students with strong analytical skills and an interest in the airline industry.

9. Intern – Cargo Operations

Location: Chicago, Illinois, United States

The Cargo Operations internship provides an opportunity to contribute to projects supporting United’s cargo business.

The role includes exposure to areas such as:

  • Logistics
  • Cargo operations
  • Digital initiatives
  • Sales strategy
  • Project management
  • Business growth

It may be particularly suitable for undergraduate students studying business or related fields who possess strong interpersonal and project-management skills.

Learn more and see other United Airlines Summer Internship Opportunities HERE.

Other Student and Early Career Opportunities at United Airlines

The eight Summer 2027 positions above are only a selection of the opportunities displayed on the Student and Early Career Jobs portal.

The current United Airlines careers page shows 45 Student and Early Career positions across multiple categories.

These categories include:

  • Corporate
  • Digital Technology
  • Student and Early Career
  • Aircraft Maintenance and Support
  • At the Airport
  • Customer Solutions
  • Flight Attendant

Because United regularly updates its vacancies, the exact number and composition of available positions can change.

Applicants should therefore review the official careers portal for the most recent vacancies before applying.

What Can Students Gain from a United Airlines Internship?

A United Airlines internship can provide much more than short-term work experience. Students can gain exposure to real business and aviation challenges while developing transferable professional skills.

United highlights several elements of its student and early-career programmes.

1. Hands-On Professional Experience

Students have the opportunity to contribute to actual projects rather than simply observing workplace activities.

This can help candidates understand how large organizations operate and how academic knowledge can be applied to real-world challenges.

2. Mentorship

United highlights mentorship and hands-on learning as part of its student and early-career experience.

Working alongside experienced professionals can help students develop industry knowledge, receive feedback and better understand possible career pathways.

3. Networking

Internships provide opportunities to interact with professionals across different teams and departments.

Building relationships during an internship can help students learn about different career paths and develop a professional network.

4. Exposure to the Aviation Industry

United Airlines operates across numerous areas beyond flying aircraft.

Students can explore careers connected to:

  • Technology
  • Cybersecurity
  • Engineering
  • Finance
  • Procurement
  • Marketing
  • Sales
  • Revenue management
  • Operations
  • Aviation safety
  • Cargo
  • Airport operations
  • Customer experience
  • Network planning

This makes United’s student opportunities relevant to students from a wide range of academic backgrounds.

5. Professional Development

United states that its student and early-career programmes are designed to help participants develop skills and connections that can support their future careers.

Interns can strengthen their:

  • Communication skills
  • Analytical abilities
  • Problem-solving skills
  • Teamwork
  • Leadership
  • Project management
  • Technical capabilities
  • Business knowledge

Digital Technology Internship Opportunities

United also has dedicated student opportunities in Digital Technology.

The company’s student careers information highlights internships involving areas such as:

  • Cybersecurity
  • Application development
  • Data analytics
  • Cloud engineering
  • Technology
  • Software development
  • Digital products

United describes its Digital Technology internships as opportunities to participate in hands-on projects over approximately 12 weeks, allowing students to develop skills in technology and innovation.

Students interested in technology careers should therefore review United’s Digital Technology opportunities alongside the broader Student and Early Career Jobs listings.

Commercial Internship Opportunities

United’s commercial internship opportunities can provide experience in areas that directly influence the airline’s business performance.

These may include:

  • Sales
  • Network planning
  • Pricing
  • Revenue management
  • MileagePlus and loyalty
  • Cargo
  • Commercial strategy

Students interested in business, economics, marketing, finance, analytics or strategic management may find these positions particularly relevant.

Finance Internship Opportunities

United also highlights opportunities in Finance.

Students can potentially gain exposure to areas such as:

  • Financial Planning and Analysis
  • Internal Audit
  • Procurement
  • Accounting
  • Financial analysis
  • Strategic decision-making

These opportunities may be particularly valuable for students pursuing finance, accounting, economics, business administration and related disciplines.

Technical Operations and Engineering Opportunities

United’s Technical Operations division provides another important pathway for students interested in aviation engineering and aircraft maintenance.

The company highlights co-op opportunities involving areas such as:

  • Aircraft maintenance
  • Line maintenance
  • Base maintenance
  • Interiors engineering
  • Avionics
  • Technical operations
  • Fleet support

These positions can provide hands-on exposure to the technical systems and processes required to keep an airline’s fleet operating safely and efficiently.

Who Can Apply for United Airlines Student and Early Career Opportunities?

Eligibility varies significantly from one vacancy to another.

There is no single qualification requirement for all 45+ positions because each role has its own academic, technical, experience and other requirements.

Generally, the opportunities are designed for:

  • Current university or college students
  • Students approaching graduation
  • Undergraduate students
  • Graduate students
  • MBA or master’s students for relevant positions
  • Recent graduates and early-career professionals for appropriate roles
  • Candidates pursuing degrees related to the advertised position
  • Candidates interested in aviation, technology, business, engineering, finance, operations and related areas

Applicants should carefully read the requirements for each individual position before submitting an application.

For example, the Masters/MBA Global Procurement internship is specifically designed for graduate-level candidates, while several of the undergraduate internships are aimed at students pursuing relevant bachelor’s degrees.

Is There an Application Deadline?

The supplied United Airlines careers page does not provide one universal application deadline for the 45 Student and Early Career positions.

Instead, individual vacancies are posted and applications may remain open for a limited period.

United’s student careers page states that internships and co-op programmes typically open during specific recruitment windows and that applications are available for a limited time. It specifically identifies September as the typical application period for Summer internships.

Therefore, applicants should not wait until a general deadline because a particular vacancy may close before then.

Important Application Advice

If you identify a position that matches your qualifications, apply as early as possible.

The safest approach is to:

  1. Review the vacancy requirements.
  2. Confirm that you meet the academic requirements.
  3. Prepare your CV/resume.
  4. Prepare any required supporting documents.
  5. Submit the application through United’s official careers portal.
  6. Monitor your email for recruitment communication.

United Airlines Recruitment Process

United explains that its student and early-career recruitment process generally progresses through several stages.

Step 1: Application Review

After an application window closes, the Campus Recruiting team reviews applications.

United indicates that applicants may hear back by email and that response times can range from approximately two weeks to two months.

Step 2: Candidate Screening

Applicants whose applications are selected may receive an invitation for a screening with a recruiter.

This stage helps determine whether the candidate proceeds to the next phase.

Step 3: Interviews

Selected candidates may interview with the hiring team.

Depending on the position, candidates may have one or two additional interviews, and some roles may include a technical assessment.

Step 4: Offer

Successful candidates receive an offer by email.

United notes that offers may be extended on a rolling basis and that timelines can vary according to the role and programme.

Step 5: Onboarding

Successful candidates begin the onboarding process before their start date.

United states that onboarding generally begins one to two months before the programme starts and may include background checks and clearance requirements.

Step 6: Programme Orientation

New hires attend United’s orientation, which takes place on the first day of the programme. Start dates can vary depending on the particular role or programme.

Learn More and Apply

How to Prepare a Strong United Airlines Internship Application

Competition for internships at major airlines can be significant. Candidates should therefore make sure their applications clearly communicate their qualifications and potential.

Tailor Your Resume

Do not use exactly the same resume for every United Airlines position.

Instead, identify the skills emphasized in the vacancy and make sure your resume demonstrates relevant experience.

For example:

  • Engineering applicants should emphasize technical projects and engineering skills.
  • Business applicants should highlight analytical and project-management experience.
  • Technology applicants should showcase programming, data, cybersecurity or technology projects.
  • Finance applicants should highlight financial analysis, accounting, modelling or related experience.
  • Supply-chain applicants should emphasize procurement, logistics and operations experience.

Highlight Academic Projects

Students often underestimate the value of academic projects.

If you have limited professional experience, include relevant university projects, research, coursework, competitions, student leadership and extracurricular activities.

Demonstrate Analytical Skills

Many of the current United internships involve analytics, strategy, operations, business intelligence or data-driven decision-making.

Candidates should demonstrate their ability to:

  • Analyze information
  • Solve problems
  • Interpret data
  • Communicate findings
  • Make evidence-based recommendations

Show Teamwork and Communication

Airline operations require collaboration across departments.

Your application should demonstrate that you can work effectively with people from different backgrounds and professional functions.

Prepare for Interviews

Research United Airlines before an interview and understand the responsibilities of the position you applied for.

Be prepared to discuss:

  • Why you want to work for United Airlines
  • Why you selected the specific internship
  • Relevant academic experience
  • Previous projects
  • Leadership experiences
  • Challenges you have solved
  • How you work in teams
  • Your career goals

Why United Airlines Can Be a Valuable Place to Start Your Career

United describes its student and early-career programmes as opportunities to build skills and professional connections while contributing to projects that move the business forward.

The company also highlights employee-run Business Resource Groups, customized intern programming and networking opportunities as components of its student experience.

For students interested in aviation, the advantage is that an airline offers career opportunities far beyond traditional aviation roles.

A student could potentially build a career in:

  • Software engineering
  • Cybersecurity
  • Data science
  • Finance
  • Accounting
  • Procurement
  • Marketing
  • Sales
  • Engineering
  • Aircraft maintenance
  • Operations
  • Airport management
  • Cargo
  • Revenue management
  • Network planning
  • Customer experience
  • Human resources

United’s corporate careers information also identifies functions such as Digital Technology, Finance, Sales, Corporate Communications, Pricing and Revenue Management, Marketing and Loyalty, Environmental Affairs, Government Affairs, Network Planning and Human Resources.

How to Find and Apply for Current United Airlines Student Jobs

Because United regularly updates its vacancies, applicants should use the company’s official careers platform to identify positions that are currently accepting applications.

The Student and Early Career section can be used to search available positions by category and other criteria.

Applicants should review the complete job description for each role before applying because requirements, locations, programme dates and other conditions can differ.

Official United Airlines Student and Early Career Jobs:
View United Airlines Student and Early Career Jobs

United Airlines Student and Early Career Programmes:
Explore United Airlines Student and Early Career Opportunities

Key Details at a Glance

Detail Information
Opportunity United Airlines Student and Early Career Jobs
Opportunity Type Jobs, Internships and Co-op Opportunities
Programme Year 2027 for the featured Summer internships
Number Listed 45 Student and Early Career positions on the supplied page
Featured Location Chicago, Illinois, United States
Fields Technology, Engineering, Business, Finance, Procurement, Safety, Sales, Revenue Management, Cargo and more
Target Group Students, graduates and early-career professionals, depending on the position
Application Deadline No single universal deadline; individual vacancies may close at different times
Application Method Online through the United Airlines Careers portal

Final Thoughts

The United Airlines Student and Early Career Jobs 2027 offer students and emerging professionals an opportunity to gain practical experience within one of the world’s major airlines.

The current listings demonstrate the breadth of careers available within the aviation industry. Students do not necessarily need to be studying aviation to benefit from United’s opportunities. Depending on the vacancy, candidates with backgrounds in engineering, business, finance, technology, food science, supply chain, analytics and other disciplines can find relevant positions.

The current Summer 2027 listings include opportunities in Technical Operations, Facilities and Ground Support Equipment Maintenance, Global Procurement, Inflight Entertainment, Corporate Safety, Sales Pricing and Strategy, Technical Operations Strategic Planning, Pricing and Revenue Management, and Cargo Operations.

Because applications are open for limited periods and there is no single deadline covering all positions, eligible candidates should review the available vacancies and apply as early as possible rather than waiting for a general closing date.

For students seeking practical experience, professional mentorship, networking and exposure to the aviation industry, a United Airlines internship or early-career position can be an important step toward building a long-term professional career.

item.content:encoded:
The Yenching Academy of Peking University Scholarship 2027 offers an exceptional opportunity for outstanding students from China and around the world to pursue an interdisciplinary graduate education focused on China at Peking University in Beijing, China.

Through the Yenching Academy, approximately 120 new students are enrolled annually, bringing together students from the Chinese Mainland and international students to study, live and learn in a highly diverse academic environment. International students make up approximately 75% of the student body, creating an environment in which scholars from different countries and academic backgrounds can engage with one another and develop a deeper understanding of China.

The programme is designed for academically outstanding students who have a strong interest in the interdisciplinary study of China and who can demonstrate extracurricular achievements, community engagement, social responsibility and leadership potential.

One of the most attractive aspects of the Yenching Academy opportunity is its generous fellowship package. Selected Yenching Scholars receive support covering tuition fees, accommodation, a monthly stipend, one round-trip travel fare and field study costs.

For the 2027 cohort, applications from international candidates and candidates from China’s Hong Kong, Macao and Taiwan regions open on September 1, 2026, with the application deadline set for November 30, 2026, at 9:00 a.m. Beijing time.

About the Yenching Academy of Peking University

The Yenching Academy is a graduate-level academic programme at Peking University, one of China’s leading universities.

The Academy brings together students from China and other parts of the world with the aim of encouraging interdisciplinary learning and deeper engagement with China.

Rather than restricting students to a single narrow academic discipline, the programme emphasizes an interdisciplinary approach to the study of China. This allows scholars with different academic backgrounds and interests to explore China from multiple perspectives.

The Academy’s international composition is also an important part of the programme. Approximately 120 new students are admitted each year, with international students accounting for roughly 75 percent of the student body.

This creates opportunities for students to develop international networks while studying alongside peers from different countries, academic disciplines and cultural backgrounds.

What Is the Yenching Academy Scholarship?

The Yenching Academy provides a generous fellowship to all scholars admitted to the programme.

The fellowship is intended to provide comprehensive financial support for selected students during their studies.

The fellowship includes:

  • Tuition fees
  • Accommodation
  • Monthly stipend
  • One round-trip travel fare
  • Field study costs

This combination of financial benefits makes the Yenching Academy particularly attractive to students seeking an internationally oriented graduate education in China with substantial financial support.

Yenching Academy 2027 Application Timeline

Applications for the 2027 cohort from international candidates and candidates from China’s Hong Kong, Macao and Taiwan regions open on:

September 1, 2026

The application deadline is:

November 30, 2026, at 9:00 a.m. Beijing time

Applicants should pay close attention to the time zone because the deadline is specified according to Beijing time, rather than the applicant’s local time.

Students should also begin preparing their application materials well before the deadline because the application requires several documents, including academic records, recommendation letters, a personal statement, a research-interest statement and proof of English proficiency where applicable.

Who Can Apply for the Yenching Academy?

The Yenching Academy welcomes applications from both Chinese Mainland candidates and students from abroad, although the application procedures differ depending on the applicant’s location and status.

The Academy generally expects applicants to demonstrate strong academic performance, intellectual curiosity, interest in China and evidence of leadership and community engagement.

Applicants should meet the following core qualifications.

1. Bachelor’s Degree or Current Bachelor’s Student

Applicants must either:

  • Hold a minimum of a Bachelor’s degree in any field; or
  • Be currently enrolled in a Bachelor’s programme and expect to receive their diploma by August of the intended enrollment year.

This means that students who have not yet completed their undergraduate education may still be eligible if they are expected to graduate by the specified date.

The Academy does not restrict the Bachelor’s degree to a particular discipline. Applicants from different academic backgrounds can therefore be considered as long as they satisfy the other requirements.

2. Outstanding Academic Record

Applicants are expected to have an outstanding academic record.

Academic excellence is an important part of the Yenching Academy selection process because the programme is designed for high-achieving students capable of engaging with rigorous graduate-level interdisciplinary study.

Applicants should therefore ensure that their transcripts accurately demonstrate their academic strengths.

3. Strong Interest in the Interdisciplinary Study of China

A key requirement is a strong interest in interdisciplinary study of China.

Applicants should be able to demonstrate why they want to study China and how their academic, professional, research or personal interests connect with the interdisciplinary focus of the Academy.

A generic interest in studying abroad may not adequately demonstrate this requirement. Applicants should instead develop a clear explanation of the questions, issues or areas concerning China that they want to explore.

4. Extracurricular Achievement and Community Engagement

The Academy also looks for applicants with a record of:

  • Extracurricular achievement
  • Community engagement
  • Social responsibility
  • Leadership potential

This means that academic performance is not the only consideration.

Applicants should demonstrate how they have contributed beyond the classroom, whether through community initiatives, student organizations, volunteering, professional activities, social-impact projects, leadership roles or other meaningful engagements.

The strongest applications should show evidence of initiative and a willingness to contribute to communities beyond one’s immediate academic environment.

5. English Proficiency

Applicants must demonstrate sufficient English proficiency unless they fall within an exemption category specified by the Academy.

The required minimum scores include:

  • IELTS Academic: Overall 7.0
  • TOEFL iBT: Overall 100
  • Cambridge English Scale (Advanced): Overall 185
  • CET 6: Overall 600
  • TEM 4: Pass level of “良好” or above

Applicants should carefully determine which English-language qualification applies to them and ensure that their test results meet the minimum requirement.

English Language Test Exemptions

Not every applicant is required to submit an English proficiency test report.

International applicants whose native language is English do not need to provide an English proficiency test report.

Applicants who have graduated from an English-taught degree programme at undergraduate level or above are also exempt from providing an English proficiency test report.

However, there is an important exception for applicants from China’s Hong Kong, Macao and Taiwan regions.

Applicants from these regions must provide an English proficiency test report even if they have attended or graduated from an English-taught degree programme.

Without an English proficiency test report, such candidates will need to take English as a Second Language after enrolling at Peking University.

For applicants from the Chinese Mainland, an English proficiency test report is a compulsory application material.

Validity Period for English Tests

The Yenching Academy specifies that English proficiency tests must have been taken after September 1, 2025.

Applicants should therefore check the date of their examination before submitting their application.

The Academy also specifies that certain alternative or modified test formats are not accepted.

The following are not accepted:

  • TOEFL MyBest Scores
  • TOEFL iBT Home Edition
  • IELTS Indicator
  • IELTS Online
  • IELTS One Skill Retake

Applicants should make sure that their English test meets the Academy’s accepted format and validity requirements.

How English Test Scores Must Be Submitted

For IELTS, TOEFL and Cambridge English tests, applicants cannot simply rely on uploading a copy of their score report where the Academy requires scores to be sent directly.

The Academy states that these scores must be sent directly by the relevant testing organizations.

When registering for the examination, applicants should select Yenching Academy of Peking University as the designated recipient of their scores.

For TOEFL applicants, the institution code is:

C488

Applicants should arrange this early enough to ensure that their scores reach the Academy before the application deadline.

Application Materials

Applicants are required to submit several materials through the Yenching Academy’s online application portal.

The application must be completed in English.

Required materials include:

  1. Completed online application form
  2. Personal statement of no more than 750 words
  3. Statement of Research Interest of no more than 1,500 words, excluding citations
  4. Curriculum Vitae
  5. Official transcript or transcripts
  6. Diploma or Certificate of Enrollment
  7. Two academic letters of recommendation
  8. Required English proficiency evidence, where applicable

Each component serves a different purpose in demonstrating the applicant’s academic preparation, research interests, leadership potential and suitability for the programme.

Personal Statement

The personal statement must be 750 words or less.

This is an opportunity for applicants to present their background and explain why they are suitable candidates for the Yenching Academy.

Rather than simply repeating information already available in the CV, applicants should use the statement to provide context around their academic journey, interests, achievements and motivation.

A strong personal statement should help admissions reviewers understand the applicant as a person and explain why the Yenching Academy is an appropriate next step.

Statement of Research Interest

Applicants must also submit a Statement of Research Interest of no more than 1,500 words, excluding citations.

This is particularly important because the Yenching Academy emphasizes interdisciplinary study of China.

Applicants should use the statement to explain the research questions or areas they are interested in exploring and demonstrate their intellectual engagement with issues concerning China.

The statement should be focused, coherent and academically grounded.

Applicants should avoid treating the statement as a generic essay about why they want to study in China. Instead, they should clearly communicate their research interests and explain the issues they would like to investigate.

Curriculum Vitae

Applicants must submit a Curriculum Vitae.

The CV should provide a clear overview of the applicant’s:

  • Academic background
  • Research experience
  • Professional experience, where applicable
  • Leadership activities
  • Extracurricular achievements
  • Community engagement
  • Relevant projects
  • Awards and accomplishments

Because the Academy specifically values extracurricular achievement, social responsibility and leadership potential, applicants should ensure that their CV captures relevant activities beyond academic qualifications.

Academic Transcripts

Applicants must provide official transcript(s).

The transcripts allow the Academy to assess the applicant’s academic record and verify educational performance.

Applicants should ensure that their academic documents are official and complete and that any required translation or certification requirements are satisfied where applicable.

Diploma or Certificate of Enrollment

Applicants must also submit the appropriate educational-status documentation.

This may be:

  • A diploma demonstrating completion of a Bachelor’s degree; or
  • A Certificate of Enrollment for applicants who are still completing their Bachelor’s programme.

Students who are currently enrolled in a Bachelor’s programme must expect to receive their diploma by August of the intended enrollment year.

Academic Recommendation Letters

Applicants must provide two academic letters of recommendation.

The recommendation letters may be written in:

  • Chinese; or
  • English.

However, the Academy imposes specific requirements concerning who may write these letters.

Peking University will only accept recommendation letters written by:

  • Full professors; or
  • Associate professors; or
  • Individuals holding equivalent academic titles.

In addition, the recommendation letters must be submitted by professors in the applicant’s intended field of study.

Applicants should therefore select their referees carefully.

A recommendation from an individual who does not meet the specified academic rank or who is not connected to the applicant’s intended field may not satisfy the Academy’s requirements.

International Student Eligibility

For the 2027 cohort, international applicants must be non-Chinese citizens with a valid passport.

This is an important nationality requirement for candidates applying through the international admissions route.

Former citizens of the Chinese Mainland, Hong Kong, Macao or Taiwan who have emigrated to another country and are applying to Peking University as international students have additional documentation requirements.

They must provide:

  • Valid passport or citizenship documents dating from before April 30, 2021; and
  • Proof of cancellation of Chinese nationality.

Applicants with complicated nationality or citizenship histories should carefully consult Peking University’s international student admissions information before submitting an application.

Applicants from Hong Kong, Macao and Taiwan

Candidates from China’s Hong Kong, Macao and Taiwan regions have a separate application process.

Applications for the 2027 Yenching Scholars cohort open on:

September 1, 2026

The deadline is:

November 30, 2026, at 9:00 a.m. Beijing time

Candidates from these regions must apply through the Yenching Academy application portal and also complete a supplementary application through the Peking University Graduate Admissions website.

Additional information is provided through Peking University’s admissions resources.

Applicants from the Chinese Mainland

The application process for candidates from the Chinese Mainland is handled through the relevant Peking University graduate admissions system.

The Academy directs Mainland Chinese candidates to the Graduate School of Peking University for additional information about the application process.

Applicants from the Chinese Mainland should therefore carefully follow the specific admissions instructions applicable to their applicant category rather than assuming that the international application procedure applies to them.

Learn More HERE

Partner University Applicants

Students and alumni of Yenching Academy’s Partner Universities must complete their home university’s internal pre-selection process before submitting an application to the Yenching Academy.

This is a particularly important requirement for candidates associated with partner institutions.

Applicants should therefore determine whether their university is included among the Academy’s partner universities and, if it is, find out whether their university has an internal nomination or pre-selection process.

Waiting until the Yenching Academy application deadline may be too late if the applicant’s university has an earlier internal deadline.

Application Portal

Candidates can submit their applications through the Yenching Academy’s online application portal.

Applicants are required to create an account before accessing additional application information and submitting their materials.

The application portal is also where applicants can find further instructions concerning the admissions process.

Applicants should make sure that all information entered into the portal is accurate and consistent with the supporting documents they submit.

APPLY HERE

Important Rule Regarding Other Degree Programmes

Peking University does not allow students to be enrolled in another degree programme while studying at the university.

Applicants who are currently enrolled in another degree programme should therefore consider this rule when planning their studies.

They should review their existing academic commitments and ensure that they understand Peking University’s requirements before accepting an offer.

Fellowship Benefits

The Yenching Academy provides a comprehensive fellowship package to all scholars.

The fellowship includes five major forms of support.

Tuition Fees

Selected scholars receive coverage of tuition fees.

This removes one of the major financial costs associated with pursuing graduate education.

Accommodation

The fellowship also provides accommodation.

This is particularly valuable for international students relocating to Beijing because housing can represent a significant component of the overall cost of studying abroad.

Monthly Stipend

Scholars receive a monthly stipend.

The supplied programme information does not specify the exact amount of the monthly stipend, so applicants should consult the admissions portal or official programme information for the current figure.

One Round-Trip Travel Fare

The fellowship includes one round-trip travel fare.

This provides travel support for the scholar and can help reduce the cost associated with travelling to and from Beijing.

Field Study Costs

The fellowship also covers field study costs.

This component is particularly relevant to the Academy’s interdisciplinary approach, as field-based academic experiences can provide scholars with opportunities to deepen their understanding of China beyond classroom-based study.

Why Study at Yenching Academy?

The Yenching Academy offers more than financial support.

Its structure is particularly suited to students who want to develop a deeper understanding of China through interdisciplinary academic inquiry.

Several characteristics make the programme distinctive.

Interdisciplinary Academic Environment

Students can explore China through different academic perspectives rather than being limited to a single disciplinary framework.

This can be particularly beneficial for students interested in complex issues that cross traditional academic boundaries.

International Community

With international students making up approximately 75 percent of the student body, the Academy provides a highly international learning environment.

Students can interact with peers from different countries and backgrounds while developing a deeper understanding of China.

Leadership Development

The Academy looks for applicants with leadership potential, community engagement and social responsibility.

This creates an environment where academic development can be combined with broader leadership and social-impact interests.

Research Opportunities

The requirement for a Statement of Research Interest highlights the programme’s emphasis on intellectual inquiry.

Students with clearly developed research interests can use the programme to investigate questions relating to China from an interdisciplinary perspective.

Field Study

The fellowship’s inclusion of field study costs provides scholars with financial support for field-based academic activities.

Such experiences can complement classroom learning and help scholars connect academic concepts with real-world contexts.

How to Prepare a Competitive Application

Because the Yenching Academy attracts high-achieving candidates, applicants should begin preparing well before the deadline.

Start With Eligibility

First, confirm that you meet the fundamental requirements.

Check:

  • Your Bachelor’s degree status
  • Your expected graduation date if you are still an undergraduate
  • Your academic record
  • Your interest in interdisciplinary study of China
  • Your extracurricular and leadership experience
  • Your English proficiency
  • Your nationality and applicant category

Develop a Clear Research Interest

The Statement of Research Interest is one of the most important components of the application.

Applicants should spend sufficient time identifying a focused area of inquiry.

Rather than selecting an extremely broad topic, consider a specific question or problem related to China that can be examined through an interdisciplinary perspective.

Choose Recommendation Writers Early

Because recommendation letters must come from full professors, associate professors or equivalent academic titles and should be from professors in the intended field of study, applicants should approach potential referees early.

This is especially important because academic referees may have multiple commitments and may require considerable time to prepare a thoughtful recommendation.

Prepare English Test Scores Early

Applicants who require an English proficiency test should avoid waiting until immediately before the deadline.

The Academy requires eligible English tests to have been taken after September 1, 2025 and does not accept several alternative test formats.

Applicants should also allow sufficient time for scores to be sent directly from the testing organization to Yenching Academy.

Review Every Document

Before submitting the application, applicants should ensure that:

  • Names are consistent across documents.
  • Academic dates are accurate.
  • Transcripts are official.
  • Recommendation letters meet the academic-rank requirements.
  • The personal statement does not exceed 750 words.
  • The Statement of Research Interest does not exceed 1,500 words excluding citations.
  • The CV is complete and professionally presented.
  • English test scores meet the required minimum where applicable.
  • Required documents have been submitted in the correct format.

Application Deadline

The application deadline for the 2027 Yenching Scholars cohort for international candidates and candidates from China’s Hong Kong, Macao and Taiwan regions is:

November 30, 2026, at 9:00 a.m. Beijing time.

Applications open on September 1, 2026.

Applicants should not wait until the final day to submit their applications because the process involves multiple supporting documents and, for some candidates, university-level pre-selection procedures.

Important Application Considerations

Applicants should keep several requirements in mind when preparing their applications.

First, students and alumni of Partner Universities must complete their university’s internal pre-selection process before submitting their Yenching Academy application.

Second, applicants who need English proficiency tests must ensure that their test was taken after September 1, 2025 and that the examination format is accepted.

Third, international candidates must satisfy the nationality requirements for international admission.

Finally, applicants should carefully follow any additional instructions displayed in the admissions portal after creating an account.

Key Facts About the Yenching Academy Scholarship 2027

Feature Details
Programme Yenching Academy of Peking University
Cohort 2027
University Peking University
Location Beijing, China
New students annually Approximately 120
International student proportion Approximately 75%
Minimum education Bachelor’s degree or current Bachelor’s student

TOEFL iBT Overall 100

Application opens September 1, 2026

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the Yenching Academy Scholarship?

The Yenching Academy provides a generous fellowship to students admitted to its interdisciplinary graduate programme at Peking University. The fellowship includes tuition fees, accommodation, a monthly stipend, one round-trip travel fare and field study costs.

Is the Yenching Academy programme open to international students?

Yes. International students make up approximately 75 percent of the Yenching Academy student body. For the international admissions route, applicants must be non-Chinese citizens with a valid passport.

What degree do I need to apply?

Applicants need at least a Bachelor’s degree in any field or must currently be enrolled in a Bachelor’s programme and expect to receive their diploma by August of the intended enrollment year.

Can students from any Bachelor’s field apply?

Yes. The Academy states that applicants may hold a Bachelor’s degree in any field.

Do I need to demonstrate leadership experience?

The Academy seeks applicants with a record of extracurricular achievement, community engagement, social responsibility and leadership potential. Applicants should therefore demonstrate meaningful involvement and evidence of initiative.

What is the English requirement?

Accepted minimum scores include IELTS Academic 7.0, TOEFL iBT 100, Cambridge English Scale 185, CET 6 600 or TEM 4 at the required “良好” or above level.

Are English tests required for everyone?

No. International applicants whose native language is English or who have graduated from an English-taught degree programme at undergraduate level or above do not need to provide an English proficiency test report. However, applicants from Hong Kong, Macao and Taiwan must provide one even if their degree was taught in English.

How many recommendation letters are required?

Two academic recommendation letters are required.

Who can write the recommendation letters?

Letters must be written by full professors, associate professors or individuals with equivalent academic titles, and they must come from professors in the applicant’s intended field of study.

How much is the monthly stipend?

The supplied programme information confirms that a monthly stipend is provided but does not specify the amount. Applicants should check the admissions portal for the current stipend amount.

Does the fellowship cover tuition?

Yes. Tuition fees are included in the fellowship.

Does the fellowship cover accommodation?

Yes. Accommodation is included.

Does the fellowship include travel support?

Yes. The fellowship includes one round-trip travel fare.

Does it cover field study?

Yes. Field study costs are included in the fellowship.

When does the 2027 application open?

Applications for international candidates and candidates from Hong Kong, Macao and Taiwan open on September 1, 2026.

When is the application deadline?

The deadline is November 30, 2026, at 9:00 a.m. Beijing time.

Can students from Partner Universities apply directly?

Students and alumni of Partner Universities must first complete their home university’s internal pre-selection process before submitting the Yenching Academy application.

Can international students who were previously Chinese citizens apply?

Potentially, but additional documentation requirements apply. Former citizens of the Chinese Mainland, Hong Kong, Macao or Taiwan who have emigrated to other countries must provide qualifying passport or citizenship documents dating from before April 30, 2021, together with proof of cancellation of Chinese nationality.

Visit HERE to learn more about the Yenching Academy of Peking University Scholarship 2027.

Conclusion

The Yenching Academy of Peking University Scholarship 2027 is a highly attractive opportunity for academically outstanding students who want to pursue an interdisciplinary graduate education focused on China in an international academic environment.

The programme combines rigorous academic study with an internationally diverse student community and places considerable emphasis on intellectual curiosity, leadership potential, community engagement and social responsibility.

For successful scholars, the financial package is particularly significant. The Yenching Academy provides tuition fees, accommodation, a monthly stipend, one round-trip travel fare and field study costs, allowing selected students to undertake their studies with substantial financial support.

Applicants should nevertheless recognize that this is a competitive programme. A strong application should go beyond meeting the minimum eligibility requirements. Candidates should present an outstanding academic record, demonstrate meaningful extracurricular and community engagement, articulate a convincing interest in the interdisciplinary study of China and submit carefully prepared application materials.

For international candidates and candidates from China’s Hong Kong, Macao and Taiwan regions, applications for the 2027 cohort open on September 1, 2026, and the application deadline is November 30, 2026, at 9:00 a.m. Beijing time.

Prospective applicants should begin preparing their transcripts, CV, personal statement, research-interest statement, recommendation letters and English-language documentation well in advance. Candidates from Partner Universities should also investigate their institution’s internal pre-selection deadline because this process must be completed before submitting the Yenching Academy application.

Overall, the Yenching Academy provides an opportunity for talented students from diverse academic and geographic backgrounds to study at Peking University, deepen their understanding of China and develop an international network while receiving substantial fellowship support.

For the latest application instructions and to begin the application process, prospective candidates should consult the official Yenching Academy admissions portal.
